mcqs.q: Health/medical informatics is best defined as the:
opts: Application of computers, communications and IT to all fields of medicine
mcqs.explain: Medical informatics is the application of computers, communications and information technology to all fields of medicine — care, education and research.

mcqs.q: Informatics evolved largely because clinicians needed to:
opts: Be more efficient, move away from paper records and reduce medication errors
mcqs.explain: Clinicians needed to be more efficient, migrate away from paper-based records, reduce medication errors and have information at their fingertips.

mcqs.q: Health informatics encompasses which sub-fields?
opts: Clinical informatics, medical informatics and bioinformatics
mcqs.explain: Health informatics includes clinical informatics, medical informatics and bioinformatics.

mcqs.q: Bioinformatics is defined as the:
opts: Analysis of biological information using computers and statistical techniques
mcqs.explain: Bioinformatics integrates biology and technology — analysing biological information using computers and statistical techniques (databases and algorithms) to accelerate research.

mcqs.q: Which is an ancillary technology that arose to augment EHR functionality?
opts: Disease registries, voice recognition and picture archiving (PACS)
mcqs.explain: Ancillary technologies include disease registries, voice recognition and picture archiving and communication systems (PACS).

mcqs.q: Which is an example of medical information that needs to be SHARED?
opts: Lab results, x-rays, vaccination and medication-allergy status
mcqs.explain: Examples of shared medical information include lab results, x-ray results, vaccination status, medication-allergy status, consultant notes and discharge summaries.

mcqs.q: The 'centerpiece' of medical informatics is the:
mcqs.explain: The EHR is considered the centerpiece of medical informatics, with potential to improve patient safety, productivity and data retrieval.

mcqs.q: EHRs are expected to improve patient OUTCOMES mainly through:
opts: Decision-support tools that reduce medication errors and embed clinical guidelines
mcqs.explain: Decision-support tools decrease medication errors and standardize care with embedded clinical guidelines, improving morbidity and mortality.

mcqs.q: Which are the main FORCES driving adoption of health information technology?
opts: Decreasing cost, improving patient safety, and standardizing/improving quality
mcqs.explain: The forces driving adoption are to decrease cost, improve patient safety, and standardize and improve the quality of care.

mcqs.q: Why has the introduction of IT into medicine been 'tumultuous'?
opts: New technologies are expensive and staff are often inadequately trained
mcqs.explain: It has been troubled because new technologies are expensive and physicians/nurses are frequently not adequately trained, with training rarely occurring in school or after graduation.

mcqs.q: MEDLINE/MEDLARS, created in the mid-1960s, were designed to:
mcqs.explain: In the mid-1960s MEDLINE and MEDLARS were created to organize the world's medical literature.

mcqs.q: In health IT history, PDAs (personal digital assistants) were largely supplanted by:
mcqs.explain: PDAs loaded with medical software were standard for residents but were quickly supplanted by smartphones like the iPhone.

mcqs.q: The goal of the Nationwide Health Information Network (NHIN) is to:
opts: Connect all EHRs, regional networks and government agencies into one system
mcqs.explain: The NHIN aims to connect all electronic health records, regional networks and government agencies into one system.

mcqs.q: The Internet is described as the backbone for:
opts: Digital medical libraries, health information exchanges and web-based EHRs
mcqs.explain: The Internet is the backbone for digital medical libraries, health information exchanges and web-based medical applications including EHRs.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of health IT by PATIENTS?
opts: Web portals, personal health records and telemedicine
mcqs.explain: Patients use online searches, web portals for personal medical information/appointments/results, personal health records and telemedicine/home telemonitoring.

mcqs.q: Clinical decision support (reminders and alerts) is a use of health IT mainly by:
mcqs.explain: Clinicians use clinical decision support (reminders and alerts), EHRs, e-prescribing, PACS and voice recognition.

mcqs.q: Syndromic surveillance and geographic information systems (GIS) to link outbreaks with geography are used by:
mcqs.explain: Public health uses incident reports, syndromic surveillance, the Public Health Information Network and GIS to link disease outbreaks with geography.

mcqs.q: Which is a COMMON goal of health IT across all key players?
opts: Reduce medical errors and duplication of tests
mcqs.explain: Common goals include reducing medical errors, improving ROI, communication and quality, reducing duplication, improving outcomes and productivity, and protecting privacy.

mcqs.q: Which is a BARRIER to health information technology adoption?
opts: Lack of interoperability and high cost
mcqs.explain: Barriers include inadequate time, cost, lack of interoperability, workflow change, privacy, legal issues, behavioral change and an inadequate workforce.

mcqs.q: 'Interoperability' as a barrier refers to:
opts: Difficulty getting different systems to exchange and use data
mcqs.explain: Lack of interoperability — systems being unable to exchange and use data with one another — is a key barrier to HIT adoption.

mcqs.q: Picture archiving and communication systems (PACS) are used to manage:
mcqs.explain: PACS (picture archiving and communication systems) store and communicate medical images such as radiographs.

mcqs.q: Which is an 'aspect' of medical informatics (a healthcare function supported by IT)?
opts: Patient safety, pharmacy, laboratory and the medical record
mcqs.explain: Aspects of medical informatics include patient care & safety, quality management, education, pharmacy, laboratory, radiology, evidence-based care, disease management and the medical record.

mcqs.q: The driving need to 'automate, collect and analyze data' arose because of:
opts: Increasing computerization and volume of medical data
mcqs.explain: As more medical information was published and more data became available through computerization, the need to automate, collect and analyze data arose.

saqs.a: The application of computers, communications and information technology to all fields of medicine (care, education & research) — the understanding, skills and tools that enable the sharing and use of information to deliver healthcare and promote health.

saqs.q: List the three branches of health informatics.
Why is the EHR considered the centerpiece of medical informatics?
saqs.a: Because it improves patient safety, productivity and data retrieval, and ultimately outcomes (morbidity & mortality) through decision-support tools that reduce medication errors and embed clinical guidelines.

saqs.q: List four historical highlights in health information technology.
saqs.a: Computers, MEDLINE/MEDLARS (1960s), the Internet, handheld tech (PDAs → smartphones), the Human Genome Project, and the Nationwide Health Information Network (NHIN).

saqs.q: Name the key players in health information technology.
List the barriers to HIT adoption.
saqs.a: Inadequate time, cost, lack of interoperability, workflow change, privacy, legal issues, behavioral change, and an inadequate workforce.
